title: Introduce provision safety margins and utilization-delta observer for Dedicated fleets
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally scale down too aggressively during short quiet windows, which leaves insufficient headroom for tenant microbursts and causes transient SLA violations. This PR introduces a configurable provisioning safety margin and a lightweight utilization-delta observer that feeds into autoscaler decisions and reporting. Goals: (1) prevent aggressive decommitment when short bursts are likely; (2) expose a sampled utilization-delta metric per-pool for post-hoc analysis and alerting; (3) keep runtime impact minimal and opt-in by config/feature-flag. What this change does: - Adds a ProvisionSafetyMargin that can be configured per-fleet and per-pool; default is 10% of committed capacity. The margin is applied as extra headroom during scale-down decisions and when computing warm-pool targets. - Adds a UtilizationDeltaObserver that samples utilization deltas across short windows (5s/30s/5m) and reports HDR-sketch-ready histograms. The observer runs with a bounded memory footprint and is off by default. - Wiring: autoscaler uses safety margin in its scale-down scoring and in the decommit cooldown calculation. The observer produces new metrics (util_delta_p50/p90/p99, util_regex_sample_rate) under the dedicated namespace. - Config and rollout: feature gated under dedicated.safety_margin.enabled and dedicated.util_observer.enabled. Cluster-wide defaults are in helm values; per-tenant overrides via FleetSpec. - Tests & validation: unit tests for margin arithmetic and observer sampling; integration test that simulates short burst followed by quiet window to validate no premature decommit; e2e gating on the Dedicated staging cluster. Migration notes: default behavior unchanged until cluster operator enables the feature; recommended gradual rollout on fleets with historical microburst patterns. Ops: expose new dashboard tiles (util-delta heatmap) and an alert recipe for sustained util_delta_p90 > 0.25 for 10m. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4721) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] metrics + dashboards instrumented - [x] feature flags + helm values - [x] docs stub in /docs/dedicated/provisioning-safety.md Related: this PR is complementary to recent warm-pool smoothing work but is intentionally orthogonal: warm-pool sizing reduces cold-starts; safety margin prevents capacity undershoot during scale decisions.

review_comments: Maya Singh: high-level LGTM — I left two questions inline: (1) can we make the observer aggregation window configurable for shorter experiments, and (2) the default 10% margin: do we have telemetry to justify that as a starting point?

Aisha Kumar: replied: made window values configurable via dedicated.util_observer.windows and added a note about choosing the default in the design doc (empirical, 95th percentile of historical short bursts across fleets).
Carlos Viteri: nit: prefer explicit constant names for the histogram tags so we don't get mismatched dashboards later. Also asked for a quick perf microbenchmark on observer CPU.
Aisha Kumar: replied: extracted histogram tag constants and added a microbench that shows <0.6% CPU on a 2k qps synthetic stream at sample_rate=0.01; results appended to the design doc.
Tomás O'Leary: requested change: make safety margin applied only to scale-down path (not scale-up). Concern: locking headroom reduces capacity for short sustained growth.

Aisha Kumar: applied change and updated tests: margin now only impacts decommit and cooldown calculations; scale-up path unaffected. Added a feature flag to enable full-path margin if operator chooses.

release_notes:
- Added configurable provisioning safety margin for Dedicated fleets to reduce risk of premature decommit during short quiet windows.
- Added Utilization-Delta observer (opt-in) to surface short-window utilization spikes for alerting and analysis.
- Feature is disabled by default; operators must enable via helm/values or FleetSpec override.
notes_for_ops: Default off. To enable: set dedicated.safety_margin.enabled=true and optionally tune dedicated.safety_margin.default_percent. For util observer: dedicated.util_observer.enabled=true and set sample_rate (e.g., 0.01). New metrics: dedicated.util_delta.p50/p90/p99 and dedicated.util_delta.sample_rate. Dashboard templates added under docs/dedicated/dashboard-templates.json
follow_up: Plan: run a 2-week canary on a subset of fleets (canary tag = safety-margin-canary) and collect util_delta histograms + SLA incidents. Next PR will add automatic recommended margin sizing based on fleet historical delta profile (ENG-4800).
